source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 956 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 956 was established by Ordinance No. 30010, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 27, 2016. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 956 is established on property located at the southwest corner of Masters Drive and Old Seagoville Road. The size of PD 956 is approximately 23 acres. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article, SIMULATED LOT means the land area that includes a new building footprint and a minimum of 25 feet around the building footprint.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 956A: development plan. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 956A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) This district is divided into two tracts, Tracts 1 and 2, as shown on the development plan. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator.

(c) The following accessory use is permitted by SUP only:

-- Accessory community center (private). (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-7.5(A) Single Family District apply.

(b) Public or private school.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is 25 feet. Lighting, retaining walls, protective athletic field netting with supporting poles, and goals are permitted in the side yard along Masters Drive.

(3) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 1.0.

(4) Height.

(A) Tract 1.

(i) Except as provided in this subparagraph, maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(ii) Structures existing before October 1, 2015 may not exceed 66 feet in height.

(B) Tract 2.

(i) Maximum height. Except as provided in this subparagraph, maximum structure height is:

(aa) 50 feet for light standards for recreational uses accessory to a public or private school;

(bb) 35 feet for netting and support poles for recreational uses accessory to a public or private school; and

(cc) 30 feet for all other structures.

(ii) Residential proximity slope. Any portion of a structure over 26 feet in height may not be located above a residential proximity slope. Exception: An elevator penthouse or bulkhead, mechanical equipment room, cooling tower, tank designed to hold liquids, ornamental cupola or dome, skylights, clerestory, visual screens that surround roof mounted mechanical equipment, amateur communications tower, parapet wall limited to a height of four feet, and an amateur communications tower may project through the residential proximity slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the residential proximity slope, whichever is less. Chimneys and vent stacks may project through the residential proximity slope to a height 12 feet above the residential proximity slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is two. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Fences For A Public Or Private School
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.109. FENCES FOR A PUBLIC OR PRIVATE SCHOOL.

(a) A maximum seven-foot wrought iron fence may be located in a required yard.

(b) Fences exceeding four feet in height and located within 25 feet of a street must be a minimum of 50 percent open. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Public or private school.

(1) Off-street parking is allowed in required yards.

(2) Screening must be provided in the locations shown on the development plan and must be a minimum height of three feet above the parking surface.

(3) Screening must be one or more of the following:

(A) Brick, stone or concrete masonry, stucco, concrete, or wood wall or fence.

(B) Earthen berm planted with turf grass or ground cover recommended for local area use by the director of parks and recreation. The berm may not have a slope that exceeds one foot of height for each two feet of width.

(C) Evergreen plant materials recommended for local area use by the director of parks and recreation. The plant materials must be located in a bed that is at least three feet wide with a minimum soil depth of 24 inches. Initial plantings must be capable of obtaining a solid appearance within three years. Plant materials must be placed a maximum of 24 inches on center over the entire length of the bed unless the building official approves an alternative planting density that a landscape authority certifies as being capable of providing a solid appearance within three years. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Landscaping And Tree Preservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.112. LANDSCAPING AND TREE PRESERVATION.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, landscaping and tree preservation must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Public or private school.

(1) Tracts 1 and 2. Simulated lot:

(A) Street frontage is not required.

(B) A maximum land area is not required.

(2) Tract 2. Tree preservation zone:

(A) Purpose. To maintain and preserve native old-growth trees for the enrichment of students and the community.

(B) Location. The tree preservation zone must be provided in Tract 2 in the location as shown on the development plan.

(C) Maintenance. The tree preservation zone must be maintained to promote the health and growing conditions of native old-growth trees.

(D) Removal. Tree removal must comply with Article X.

(E) Credit. Existing trees located within the tree preservation zone may be counted toward tree replacement requirements for Tract 1 at a one caliper inch to one caliper inch ratio.

(F) New construction.

(i) New construction is prohibited within the tree preservation zone.

(ii) New construction must be located a minimum of 20 feet from the edge of a tree canopy for any tree located within the tree preservation zone.

(iii) Construction or restoration of a perimeter fence or signs identifying tree species within the tree preservation zone is allowed.

(G) Pedestrian amenities. Permeable walking paths and bench seating are permitted within the tree preservation zone. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.113. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Public or private school.

(1) In general.

(i) Attached signs.

(aa) Attached non-premise signs are prohibited.

(bb) Signs and words on the signs must be parallel to and may project a maximum of 18 inches from the building surface to which they are attached.

(cc) The maximum effective area for all attached signs on each facade is 25 percent of the total area of the facade.

(dd) A maximum of eight words are allowed on each facade. Maximum letter height is 11-feet two-inches.

(ii) Monument signs. Monument signs are restricted to 10 feet in height and 12 feet in width.

(2) Tract 1. Two detached premise signs are permitted in Tract 1.

(3) Tract 2. One detached premise sign is permitted in Tract 2. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 30010)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-956.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 30010)
